Obituaries

John F. Arguello, Stella Verven Kalemeris, Frank Antoine Merriweather, Jerry Reinlieb, Frederick Richard Schrade, Calogero Terrano, Christine Sara Lynn Thompson (Junghans)
(Freepik.com)
By Eric Harvey, eric@peekskillherald.com
August 21, 2026

John F. Arguello

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 24:45
Instaread

John Arguello, a cherished husband, devoted father, and beloved friend, passed away peacefully on August 17, 2026. Born on May 18, 1974, in Quito, Ecuador, John was the cherished son of Raul Sr. and Betty Arguello. He was preceded in death by his father Raul Sr. and his brothers, John Patricio and Raul Jr.

John’s life was a tapestry woven with love, dedication, and an enduring spirit of generosity.  Raised in Peekskill, New York, he graduated from Peekskill High School in 1992. Soon after, he embarked on a journey of service and honor by joining the United States Navy. From 1992 to 1994, John served aboard the USS Saratoga (CV-60) during Operation Desert Storm, navigating the Mediterranean Sea with courage and steadfast resolve. As an Aviation Boatswains Mate, he was instrumental in maintaining aircraft launch and flight deck operations, showcasing his exemplary skill and dedication.

It was years later when John met the love of his life, Jessica, whom he married on September 29, 2012. Together, they built a beautiful family, raising their three cherished children, Lorenzo, Olivia, and Giancarlo. John was a devoted father whose love for his children was boundless and unwavering. John’s entrepreneurial spirit flourished as he pursued his passions for food, music, and community.

He was the proud owner and operator of several successful businesses, including Cupoccino Cafe, La Tasca, Platinum City Limo, and Platinum Entertainment. A man of many talents, his ventures were a reflection of his vibrant personality and commitment to bringing joy to others. A dedicated volunteer firefighter with Columbian Engine Company No. 1 in Peekskill, John embodied the spirit of service and selflessness.

His infectious smile, quick wit, and unwavering charm made him a beloved figure in his community. He had an innate ability to listen and offer advice, always putting others before himself, and ensuring the well-being of those around him. John’s love for life was evident in his passions for sports, cars, music, and dancing. He cherished entertaining his family and friends, creating lasting memories filled with laughter and joy.

His heart was as expansive as his love for his family, and he leaves behind his beloved wife, Jessica, his children, Lorenzo, Olivia, and Giancarlo, his mother, Betty Arguello, and his dear sisters Jenny Boustani(John) Nora Ryan (Mike), and Marie Basilone(Steve), along with his loving nieces and nephews.

A service to honor John’s life will be held on August 22, 2026, at 10:30 AM at St Kateri Tekakwitha Church, located at 1925 Route 82, Lagrangeville, NY.

In lieu of flowers, the family kindly requests that donations be made to Sparrow.s Nest,

Donation Form an organization close to John’ heart.

  • Sourced from William G. Miller & Son Funeral Home Inc

Stella Verven Kalemeris

Stella Kalemeris died on August 12, 2026, at her home in Albuquerque, leaving the world in which she lived for 99 and a half years.

Born Stella James Verven in Poughkeepsie, NY, to James and Pitsa Trampas Verven shortly after they immigrated from the Peloponnesus region of Greece, she grew up in Poughkeepsie’s tight knit Greek community with her siblings, cousins Effie and Daisy Verven and many friends. She deftly navigated the dual responsibilities of first generation children, who had to both preserve their cultural heritage and become assimilated Americans. She was immersed in all the activities of the Greek Orthodox Church. She learned Greek history, the traditional dances and customs, and spoke, read and wrote Greek fluently. On the American side, she was a top student throughout her public school education.

Her childhood and adolescence were defined by the Great Depression and Second World War. She graduated with Poughkeepsie High School class of 1944, an event that marked the departure of most of the boys to fight the war. Several did not come back, including a very special friend who was killed at the Battle of the Bulge.

After high school she embarked on a seven-year career at the Poughkeepsie Journal newspaper. On November 4, 1951, at the Greek Orthodox Church in Poughkeepsie, she married Soterios Kalemeris of Peekskill, NY. She moved there, contributed to the Baby Boom, and took on the role of wife and mother, happily channeling the likes of June Cleaver, Harriet Nelson, Donna Reed and all the other perfect TV housewives of the era. She loved that role and gave her children the quintessential Baby Boomer childhood: a kid-centered universe, complete with all the classic toys and experiences that hallmarked that generation.

She was a born leader. She joined the Hellenic Ladies Society, a philanthropic group of Greek women, and served as president for several terms. The Thursday night “meetings” with her dear friends Pauline Piliouras, Georgia Anton, Freda Voonasis, Athena Kerasiotis and all the other good Greek ladies of Peekskill were a hoot! Along with her very good friend Ellen Rinzivillo, she signed up for Den Mother with Uriah Hill Cub Scout Pack #20. They took an unorthodox approach to their duties and their escapades often left the Cub Master speechless. She was a force to be reckoned with: in 1963 she organized the class parents into a unified front to remove her son’s woefully inadequate fourth grade teacher from her position, taking on the school board and powerful teachers union in the process. The name Mrs. Singer (the stringent replacement teacher) became emblematic of her victory, and she invoked it frequently over the next 60 years.

When her children were old enough to fend for themselves she joined the family business, which was, of course, restaurants. Over the next two decades she did every job from waitress to short order cook to manager. Her sharp mind worked overtime behind the scenes as she calculated income and expenses, profits and losses, weekly payroll, monthly sales tax and all the other financial details that keep a business going. And all at a time before electronic spreadsheets were even an idea.

After her husband died she moved to Clifton, VA, and then to Rio Rancho. In New Mexico, she found a new Greek community with the same closeness and family spirit as the one in which she grew up. She attended St. George Greek Orthodox Church in Albuquerque, and was a member of their chapter of the Ladies Philoptochos Society.

She is survived by her children Maria Paulson and Arthur Kalemeris, grandsons Jason and Stephen Paulson and their wives Blair and Deborah respectively, great-grandchildren Evan, Joshua, Stella, Brooklyn, Dean and Scarlett Paulson, sister-in-law Georgia Verven, nieces Patricia Miller, Patricia Uhl, Nancy Simou, nephew Stephen Verven, godchildren Byron Piliouras and Patricia Pappas, and her little buddy, Leo.

She was predeceased by her husband, sons-in-law Richard Paulson and Kenneth Hall, brothers Stephen and Angelo Verven, sister Electra Danko, nephews Jamie Verven and John Danko, sister-in-law Maria Verven and brother-in-law John Danko.

Her children extend their sincere appreciation to the Ambercare Hospice team that provided such competent, comprehensive and gentle care for their mother over many months. They were the bright light that illuminated the path of her final journey.

In lieu of flowers, kindly consider a donation to St. George Greek Orthodox Church of Albuquerque.

  • Sourced from French Funerals & Cremations

Frank Antoine Merriweather

Frank Antoine Merriweather, a devoted husband, father, son, grandfather, brother, and friend, passed away, leaving behind a lifetime of memories, accomplishments, and love that will forever remain in the hearts of those who knew him.

Frank was born on October 16, 1962, in Tarrytown, New York, to Pearl and Frank Merriweather. He was baptized at Mt. Lebanon Church in Peekskill, New York, under the guidance of Reverend Drake.

Frank is predeceased by his father, Frank Merriweather, both maternal and paternal grandparents, and a nephew. 

He graduated from Peekskill High School in 1980 and went on to attend Morrisville College before answering the call to serve his country.

Frank proudly served four honorable years in the United States Army. During his military career, he distinguished himself through his dedication, discipline, and commitment to excellence. He worked in the JAG Dept. He was recognized with numerous awards, including Soldier of the Month and the Good Conduct Medal. While stationed in Germany, Frank studied the German language, embracing the opportunity to learn about another culture while serving his country.

Following his honorable discharge from the Army, Frank continued his education and earned his Bachelor of Arts degree from SUNY Empire. He later earned a degree in Chemical Dependency Counseling. Education, service, leadership, and helping others were important parts of Frank’s life, and he carried those values with him throughout the years. His accomplishments and recognitions reflected not only his abilities, but also his determination to make a difference in the lives of others.

Frank was a man who cherished his family and the memories they created together. He leaves to cherish his memory his beloved wife, Sheila Merriweather; his loving daughter, Alaina Session, Peekskill, NY; granddaughter of Shaynna Session, Buffalo, NY, Peekskill; his beloved mother, Pearl Merriweather, Montgomery, Al. his sister, Dana (Gerald) Belin; his brother, Vernon Keith (Marcy) Merriweather; his brother, Ronald Bell; his sister, Shawnye (Ronald) Johnson; mother in law Patricia Haggerty, Greenville, New York, Brother, Jemel White (Deceased) Bonus sister Joi White, ATL, Bonus Brother Derrick Jackson of White Plains, Niece Kiara Merriweather, Bowie Md. nephew, Kerron Merriweather Casiano Cortlandt, niece Brandi Belin, Peekskill, niece Brittany Belin, Peekskill, niece, Azaria Johnson, D.C., nephew Jaden Johnson, Peekskill, NY, nephew, Christian Jones, Cortlandt, NY. Great-nephew, Boston Bowie, MD., A stepsons, Michael Holliman of Greenville, NY, his granddaughters, I Kali, Kamai, Marleigh, Greenville, NY. Nevaeh, Matteo, Rafael, Peekskill, NY; Lorenzo, Mexico; extended family members; and close friends.

Frank’s life was defined by service, perseverance, family, and love. He was a man who experienced much, accomplished much, and left an impression on the people fortunate enough to know him. His family will remember not only the things he accomplished, but the moments shared, the stories told, the laughter, and the love that made him who he was.

Frank knew something about everything; that he was nicknamed the professor. His passions were sports, playing golf, swimming, and good food. He loved to travel and experience new things. He was the epitome of what living life was about.

Though he is no longer with us in person, Frank’s spirit and legacy will continue through his family, the lives he touched, and the memories he leaves behind. His journey may have come to an end, but the love he gave and the memories he created will remain forever.

May Frank Antoine Merriweather aka “The Governor” “Frank Star” rest peacefully, knowing that he was deeply loved, greatly respected, and will never be forgotten.

Visitation will be held at the United Methodist Church of Peekskill, 1040 Main St, Peekskill, NY 10566 on Saturday, August 22, 2026, from 12:00 pm to 1:00 pm.

Celebration of Life to begin immediately following visitation at 1:00 pm.

Private Cremation Ceremony to Follow.

In lieu of flowers, donations in Frank’s memory can be made to St. Jude Children’s Research Hospital 

  • Sourced from Joseph F. Nardone Funeral Home

Jerry Reinlieb

Jerry Reinlieb, a Cortlandt Manor resident, passed away peacefully on August 9, 2026, surrounded by his family and a house full of love, leaving behind a legacy of warmth, laughter, and light.

Jerry was born on July 1, 1945, in Williamsburg, Brooklyn, to Sue and Alex Reinlieb. He grew up alongside his brother, Joel, and attended the High School of Art and Design in New York City. It was there that Jerry’s lifelong passion for photography took shape—a passion he turned into a fulfilling professional career and continued to cherish throughout his life. As a young photographer, Jerry seamlessly combined his eye for imagery with his love of music. In 1965, he captured history through his lens, photographing Bob Dylan during his landmark concert at Forest Hills Tennis Stadium in Queens. Music remained a cornerstone of Jerry’s life, with favorites ranging from The Kingston Trio and Simon & Garfunkel to Neil Diamond and Bruce Springsteen.

Jerry married Ilene Reinlieb in 1968, and together they had two children, Stacy Reinlieb LaMuniere, born in 1970, and David Reinlieb, born in 1974. Jerry spent much of his career as a photographer at New York Medical College. Never one to fully step away from his craft or his work ethic after retiring from NYMC, he went on to work at Sam’s Camera in Mount Kisco and later at the Sony Store in Manhattan.

Jerry and Ilene eventually divorced, and in 1990 Jerry married Patricia Yarusso. Together they welcomed their daughter, Hayley Reinlieb, in 1994.

While photography was a central passion, Jerry’s enthusiasm for life spanned many interests. In his younger years, he was a strong swimmer, a skilled water skier, and an avid hiker and cyclist. During his years at New York Medical College, he loved playing on the company softball team. Jerry also had a deep appreciation for the quiet beauty of the world around him—particularly hummingbirds, owls, lighthouses, and waterfalls. He loved dogs, enjoyed smoking his pipe for many years, and was a faithful fan of Star Trek, M*A*S*H, and Deadwood. Some of his happiest moments were the simplest ones: sharing laughs and catching up on Seinfeld with his dear friends and neighbors of more than 25 years, Bob and Martha Klein.

More than any hobby or professional achievement, Jerry will be remembered for the person he was. Warm, kind, thoughtful, and remarkably modest, he had an effortless way of making people feel at ease. He possessed a sharp wit, a fantastic sense of humor, and a wonderfully sarcastic edge that kept everyone laughing. Negativity and pessimism simply weren’t in his nature; even throughout his illness, Jerry maintained the positivity, sharp humor, and warmth that defined his entire life. Above all, he was exceptionally proud to be a grandfather to his two grandsons, Ayden and Jace.

Jerry was predeceased by his parents, Sue and Alex Reinlieb. He is survived by his wife, Patricia Reinlieb; his children, Stacy Reinlieb LaMuniere and her husband, Michael; David Reinlieb and his wife, Chantal Kullman Reinlieb; and Hayley Reinlieb and her life partner, Jeffrey Robinson; his beloved grandsons, Ayden and Jace; his brother, Joel Reinlieb, and his wife, Seena; and his niece, Lori Busch.

There will be no traditional funeral service. Instead, Jerry’s family will hold a Celebration of Life gathering at a future date, where family and friends can gather to share stories, laugh, and celebrate a life that brought immeasurable joy to everyone who knew him.

  • Sourced from Joseph F. Nardone Funeral Home

Frederick Richard Schrade

It is with profound sadness that we announce the passing of Frederick Richard Schrade, who passed away on Sunday, August 8, 2026.

Frederick was a beloved and devoted husband, father, grandfather, businessman, collector, car enthusiast, and, perhaps above all, storyteller.

To his family, he was so much more.

Born in Yonkers, New York, on November 26, 1946, Frederick was raised in a traditional Italian family and remained immensely proud of his heritage and his Yonkers roots throughout his life. Family was at the center of his world from the very beginning. He was devoted to his mother, father, aunts, uncles, and cousins, and later loved sharing stories about those years with his own children and grandchildren. And when Frederick told a story, he always knew exactly how much embellishment it needed to make it just a little bit better.

Frederick proudly served his country in the United States Army during the Vietnam War. The relationships and friendships he formed during that chapter of his life remained important to him, and he maintained some of them until his passing.

Sharp, quick-witted, confident, and when he was younger fast driver, Frederick earned the nickname “Fast Freddy.” It fit him perfectly. He had a big personality, an unmistakable voice, a collection of unforgettable catchphrases, and a presence that filled a room. Those who loved him often found themselves doing their best impression of him—and always out of affection. Frederick was the kind of person you met once and remembered forever.

He was also the type of “know-it-all” you actually listened to—because when Frederick knew something, he knew it well.

Frederick’s greatest pride, however, was his family. Everything revolved around his beloved wife of 54 years, Barbara Schrade, and his two sons, Luke Schrade and Joseph Schrade. He was an incredibly proud father who wanted nothing more than to provide for his family, spend time with them, and give them a life filled with experiences and memories.

Whether he was coaching his boys, traveling for their sports, creating unimaginable Christmas mornings, or simply making sure his family had everything they needed, Frederick loved to give. Providing for the people he loved was never an obligation to him—it was one of the ways he showed his love.

Frederick built F&F Electrical Contractor Corp., a business that became an important part of his life’s work. He brought both of his sons into that world and shared his knowledge, work ethic, and experience with them. His son Joseph would ultimately follow in his father’s footsteps and continue in the electrical contracting business.

Outside of work, Frederick had an appreciation for the things that captured his interest. He was an avid collector and a lifelong car enthusiast, and when something fascinated him, he wanted to know everything about it. He had strong opinions, endless knowledge, and usually a story to go along with both.

But Frederick may have been at his very best sitting around a table surrounded by family.

He was the ultimate storyteller. He could hold everyone’s attention, retelling stories everyone had heard before but somehow still wanted to hear again. There would be laughter, interruptions, exaggerations, arguments over exactly how something happened—and, inevitably, another story.

Frederick was loved and respected by so many people throughout his life. He was generous, charismatic, funny, fiercely devoted to his family, and completely and unapologetically himself.

To his son Luke, “My dad was always my hero. I always wanted and still want to be like my dad.”

That may be the simplest way to describe the enormous place Frederick held in the lives of those closest to him.

Frederick Richard Schrade—Fast Freddy—made an unforgettable first impression and lived an unforgettable life. His stories, his voice, his sayings, his generosity, his larger-than-life personality, and most importantly, his love for his family will live on in everyone who had the privilege of knowing him.

Visitation will be held at Joseph F. Nardone Funeral Home, 414 Washington Street, Peekskill, NY 10566, on Friday, August 14, 2026, from 4:00 pm to 8:00 pm.

Chapel Service to take place on Friday, August 14, 2026, at 5:00 pm during the hours of visitation.

Entombment and Rendering of Military Funeral Honors, the Playing of Taps, followed by the Flag Folding and Presentation Ceremony  to take place at Woodlawn Cemetery, 4199 Webster Ave, Bronx, NY 10470 on Saturday, August 15, 2026 at 11:00 am. 

  • Sourced from Joseph F. Nardone Funeral Home

Calogero Terrana

It is with sadness that we announce the passing of our devoted husband, father, and nonno Calogero Terrana on August 18, 2026, at the age of 90.  

Born on March 24, 1936, in Favara, Sicily, he lived through wartime and austerity.  After serving in the Italian military, he emigrated to the US to join his family in Pleasantville, NY.  He worked at the experimental chicken farm in South Salem, NY, and GM Tarrytown.  In 1969, he married Serafina Strazzeri in Giardini-Naxos, Sicily, and brought her to the US.  They moved with their three children to their current home in Peekskill in 1974. Often working two jobs, he was a carpenter with the North Atlantic Carpenters and worked nights at Reader’s Digest.  

He is survived by his devoted wife of 57 years, Serafina Terrana; daughter Maria Levy (Peter), son Joseph Terrana (Julie), daughter Cynthia Terrana-Astrologo (Carlo), and grandchildren Aliya, Michael, Rebecca, Mikayla, Cassandra, Francesco, and Aria; brothers Salvatore Terrana (Jane) and Dominic Terrana (Judith), and sister-in-law Joan Terrana; and many loving nieces, nephews, and cousins. He was predeceased by parents Giuseppe and Rosa Terrana, sisters Rita Terrana, M.S.C, Antonia Cannizzaro, and Rosalia Terrana, and brother Gaspare Terrana. 

He was a presence that all would gravitate to with his gregarious and supportive demeanor. He could rule a dance floor and be the life of the party. He was a charismatic storyteller with a contagious sense of humor.  If you weren’t laughing with him, you were engaged and listening to his many life stories of the time he spent in Malvizzo. He loved the endless family parties and hosted many through the decades.  He was deeply loyal to his family and friends and loved and respected by all who knew him.  

Visitation waswill be held at Joseph F. Nardone Funeral Home on Thursday, August 20, 2026, from 3:00 pm to 8:00 pm.

Funeral Mass waswill be held at the Church of the Assumption on Friday, August  21, 2026 at 10:00 am.

Entombment to Follow at Gate of Heaven Cemetery, Hawthorne, NY.

  • Sourced from Joseph F. Nardone Funeral Home

Christine Sara Lynn Thompson (Junghans)

Christine Sara Lynn Thompson, 53, of Carmel, New York, passed away unexpectedly on August 12, 2026. Born on August 22, 1972, Christine was the daughter of the late Reverend John Junghans and Marjorie Stover Junghans. She is survived by her two daughters, Tessa and Thea Thompson, and their father, Tony Thompson. Additionally, she is survived by her brother, Mark Junghans, sister-in-law Sara Junghans, and their children: Emma, Miya, and Will. Christine also leaves behind her niece and nephew, Henry and Dagny Junghans, and her devoted best friend, Dina DiPaola-Gulli, and her family. Christine was preceded in death by her brothers, Michael and Jay Junghans. She was a loving mother, sister, and friend to many. 

ChristineChristen graduated from SUNY Geneseo with a bachelor’s degree in education and later obtained a master’s degree in education. She worked as a tenured elementary school teacher at Hillcrest Elementary School. She spent much of her free time being a dance mom, volunteering at her church, Emmanuel Evangelical Lutheran Church and honing her cooking skills.

Christine was devoted to her daughters, always their biggest supporter, whether at dance recitals, choral performances or school musicals. For many years, she planned fellowship events at her church. The church community always looked forward to the annual Easter egg hunt, Vacation Bible School and many coffee hours. 

Visitation will be from 4:00 PM – 8:00 PM at Beecher Flooks Funeral Home, Pleasantville, NY, on Thursday, August 20, 2026. Funeral services for Christine will be at Emmanuel Evangelical Lutheran Church, Pleasantville, NY, on Friday, August 21, 2026, at 10AM. 

Christine was a loving parent who always put her daughters first. Many people have asked how they can help during this sad time. Friends have set up a GoFundMe to support Tessa and Thea. All money raised will go directly to their education, and future needs. To access the GoFundMe, click here. https://gofund.me/6fcf82c7d

We are immensely saddened by the loss of Christine; she will be greatly missed by her family and friends. Please keep Tessa and Thea in your prayers.

Several people left touching messages for Christine on a tribute wall posted on her obituary.

Symone Griffin commented: “Ms. Junghans was my third grade teacher (2001-2002) and she was the very first teacher that looked like me. She was a force to be reckoned with, but deeply cared about all the students that passed through her classroom. I was her student during 9/11 and she made a very stressful and scary day easier for our little minds. I underwent three operations during her time as my teacher and she never made me feel like I was a burden upon returning to class…”

Simone Wright commented: “My son had Ms. Thompson this past school year. She pushed him to be his best, not just academically but personally. We will forever be grateful. While we are shocked and saddened I can only imagine what her girls must feel. I hope they find solace in knowing how proud they made her feel.”

Emily Díaz commented: “’A great soul serves everyone all the time. A great soul never dies.’ — Maya Angelou. Christine was one of these souls. She often went out of her way to make others feel welcomed, accepted and cherished. She was very proud of her beautiful daughters Thea and Tessa, and will share their accomplishments. She was a great woman with a beautiful soul, hence why Christine was one of my most favorite people and colleagues.”

About the Contributor
Eric Harvey, News Reporter
Eric Harvey joined the staff of the Peekskill Herald as a full-time reporter in September 2024, covering a general assignment beat that includes the City of Peekskill and The Board of Education. Harvey, 26, of Stamford, C.T., previously was a politics and crime reporter at the Bronx Riverdale Press, where he was the recipient of a New York Press Association Better Newspaper Contest award for a 2023 feature story on the man who co-wrote Martin Luther King’s I Have A Dream speech. A graduate of Champlain College in Vermont, Harvey said he likes working in community journalism because it allows for making a difference. “Peekskill is a beautiful and diverse city with rich story potential,” Harvey said. “I look forward to continuing to get to know the community better and shine a spotlight on community members’ needs and interests.” Have a tip?
